items.title: A.I. and Our Economic Future
items.desc: Charles I. Jones (NBER WP 34779, rev. June 2026). Argues AI could be the most transformative technology of the modern era and may accelerate growth beyond the ~2%/yr the US has held for 150 years, though "weak links" temper the acceleration.

items.title: AI in Science
items.desc: Agrawal, McHale & Oettl (NBER WP 34953, Mar 2026). Models AI's effect on the knowledge-production function, framing it as augmenting search over large combinatorial spaces.

items.title: Teaching Economics to the Machines
items.desc: NBER WP 34713 (Jan 2026). Examines how economic reasoning can be taught to and elicited from machine-learning systems.

items.title: AI Patents in the United States and China
items.desc: NBER WP 35022 (2026). Builds a classifier to measure AI patents and documents rapid growth in both countries, with China surpassing the US in recent annual counts.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services: Applications, Opportunities, and Risks
items.desc: Aryan Choudhary (SSRN, May 2026). Weighs speed/scalability gains against algorithmic bias and black-box opacity; argues durable advantage comes from pairing algorithmic efficiency with governance and human oversight.

items.title: The Role of AI and Machine Learning in Algorithmic Trading
items.desc: Ananya (SSRN, Apr 2026). Reviews supervised/reinforcement learning and NLP trading systems and their effects on execution efficiency, price discovery, and liquidity.

items.title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Finance: A Comprehensive Survey
items.desc: arXiv (q-fin). Surveys autonomous, multi-agent financial systems, noting the literature remains fragmented across CS, economics, and operations.

items.title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning in Computational Finance: A Systematic Review
items.desc: arXiv (q-fin). Systematic review of ML/DL methods across pricing, forecasting, and risk in computational finance.

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: OM Forum — Supply Chain Management in the AI Era: A Vision Statement
items.desc: M&SOM. Vision statement from the OM community organizing AI–supply-chain interaction across five layers: intelligence, execution, strategy, human, and infrastructure.

items.title: Synergizing Artificial Intelligence and Operations Research
items.desc: INFORMS Journal on Data Science (2026). Argues many high-impact AI applications (supply chain, transportation, humanitarian logistics) rest on problems that are fundamentally operations, and shows how OR and AI reinforce each other.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Firm Resilience: Evidence from Natural Disaster Shocks
items.desc: Information Systems Research. Empirical evidence that AI adoption improves firm resilience to disaster shocks.

items.title: Has China obtained the world's most important machine?
items.desc: The Economist (Jul 5). On the geopolitics of advanced chipmaking equipment central to the AI race.

items.title: America should not imprison frontier AI
items.desc: The Economist (Jul 2). Leader arguing against overly restrictive US controls on access to the most powerful AI models.

items.title: Donald Trump's AI regime is opaque, unpredictable—and unsustainable
items.desc: The Economist (Jun 30). Analysis of the business and policy uncertainty created by the current US approach to AI governance.

items.title: The Small-Business Owners Managing Whole Armies of A.I. Employees
items.desc: NYT (Jun 4). How small businesses are deploying fleets of AI agents to do the work of staff.

items.title: A New Ad Campaign Tries to Make A.I. a Little Less Scary
items.desc: NYT (Jun 4). On marketing efforts to reshape public perception of consumer AI.
